title: LE10: the full-face support variant
summary: Build a swept quadratic elliptic plate, distinguish the full-face ESRD support from original NAFEMS LE10, and compare the correct stress at D with an independent reference.

steps.title: Start the LE10 support variant
steps.explain: Build the ESRD full-face-support variant of NAFEMS LE10 in our own Commands. It is a thick elliptic plate under pressure, and its independent stress reference is −5.25 MPa. The original NAFEMS mid-plane-line support is a different boundary condition with a −5.38 MPa reference; this guide does not claim to run that original case.

steps.title: Units and signs
steps.explain: Use metres, newtons and MPa. Compression is negative stress. A positive pressure acts into the selected surface.

steps.title: Elastic plate material
steps.explain: Use E = 210 GPa and ν = 0.3, as in the published reference. This is linear static elasticity; no density or time step is needed.

steps.title: Map the two ellipses and sweep the thickness
steps.explain: The quarter-annulus lies between ellipses with semi-axes (2, 1) m and (3.25, 2.75) m. A mapped 12 × 12 base follows both curves exactly; eight quadratic layers span the 0.6 m thickness. mesh.set creates the implicit plate Body. Thickness refinement matters for the upper-surface stress, not just the number of elements around the hole.

steps.title: Assign the Material
steps.explain: The implicit swept Body is named plate. Assign the Material normally; it is the same kind of analysis target as a Body made by a geometry Command.

steps.title: Mirror the x cut
steps.explain: The x = 0 cut is a true reflection plane. Remove ux only so the plate can bend in z.

steps.title: Mirror the y cut
steps.explain: The y = 0 cut removes uy only. Point D is on this cut at x = 2 m, on the inner ellipse.

steps.title: State the support variant explicitly
steps.explain: Fix ux, uy and uz over the WHOLE outer elliptical face. This is ESRD’s full-face variant. Holding uz only on the outer mid-plane line would permit a different through-thickness displacement field and require the original −5.38 MPa reference.

steps.title: Load the top surface
steps.explain: A uniform 1 MPa pressure acts down onto z = 0.6 m. The lower surface is unloaded.

steps.title: Define the static Step
steps.explain: Use both reflection constraints, the full outer-face support and the top pressure. A support is part of the benchmark definition, not a numerical knob to tune until the answer matches.

steps.title: Solve and probe point D
steps.explain: Probe stress component 1 (σyy) at [2 m, 0 m, 0.6 m]. The checked quadratic mesh gives about −5.234 MPa, within 0.31% of the independently published full-face reference −5.25 MPa. Do not probe the mid-plane or use von Mises: both answer different questions.

steps.title: Fit the plate
steps.explain: Fit the curved plate in the viewer; then inspect the upper inner corner and the full outer-face support. Fit changes the camera, never the Model or Result.

steps.title: Stress, refinement and the right reference
steps.explain: A plausible number is not enough: check its component, coordinate, interpolation and support definition.
steps.theory:
The reported quantity is $\sigma_{yy}(D)$ at $D=(2,0,0.6)\,\mathrm m$. For the **full-face-support variant**, ESRD reports **−5.25 MPa**. Our 12 × 12 × 8 Hex20 mesh gives about **−5.234 MPa**, an error of 0.30%. A 6 × 6 × 2 quadratic mesh gives about −5.489 MPa (4.56% error): refining both the plane and thickness moves toward the independent reference. The automated tutorial check repeats that coarse/fine comparison.

Run `query.probe` with `step: "static"`, `field: "stress"`, `component: 1`, `at: ["2 m", "0 m", "0.6 m"]`. The probe interpolates recovered nodal stress; it is not the raw value at a Gauss point. Inspect reaction balance as well as the local stress.

**Why not −5.38 MPa?** The original NAFEMS LE10 support restrains in-plane motion over the outer face but vertical motion only along its mid-plane line. The present guide restrains all components over the entire outer face. The existing bundled example has the same variant; neither this tutorial nor that example establishes the original line-supported result. A coarse full-face mesh landing close to −5.38 MPa is discretization error, not proof of equivalent supports.

**Other solvers:** Hex20 corresponds to a quadratic 20-node solid (for example Abaqus C3D20 or Ansys SOLID186); Nastran likewise uses a quadratic CHEXA. The mirrored cuts use normal-component constraints, and the variant’s rim is a three-component SPC. Compare the actual boundary conditions and recovery convention rather than assuming identical element names imply identical results.

Sources: [ESRD StressCheck Benchmarks Guide, pp. 29–31](https://www.esrd.com/wp-content/uploads/dlm_uploads/Benchmarks-Guide-Standard-NAFEMS-Benchmarks-Linear-Elastic-Tests.pdf); [SimScale LE10 workflow reference](https://www.simscale.com/projects/wilHo/thick_plate_under_pressure_nafems_le10_1/). Text, Commands and visualizations here are re-authored; the original vendor tutorials are not embedded.
